raw:
I remember a compost pail that had tipped over by a fence. The lid was wedged against the fence, and there were rotting peaches stuck to the rim. The peaches were unpleasant enough, but then I noticed the maggots underneath the pail. That was the part that really disgusted me—all that little movement together. I wanted to look away, but my eyes kept going back to it.

And the peaches still looked enough like peaches that I kept thinking of them as something you could eat, even while looking at what they’d turned into. Somehow that made it worse. I remember feeling my stomach turn and wanting to put some distance between myself and the pail. It’s the maggots I picture first, though, more than anything else.
